examples.ko: 영화 속 패잔병들이 산길을 힘없이 걸어가요.
examples.en: The defeated soldiers in the movie walk wearily along the mountain path.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어지고 나니 제가 꼭 패잔병 같아요.
examples.en: After failing the exam, I feel just like a defeated soldier.

examples.ko: 그는 패잔병처럼 어깨를 늘어뜨리고 집에 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: He came home with drooping shoulders like a beaten soldier.

examples.ko: 역사책에서 패잔병이 마을로 숨어든 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read in a history book about stragglers from the defeated army hiding in a village.

examples.ko: 경기에 진 선수들이 패잔병의 모습으로 나갔어요.
examples.en: The players who lost the game walked out looking like defeated soldiers.

examples.ko: 패잔병 같은 표정 짓지 말고 힘내요!
examples.en: Don't look so defeated, cheer up!

explain: 원래는 전쟁에서 진 군인을 말하지만, 일상에서는 시험이나 경기에서 져서 풀이 죽은 사람을 비유할 때 더 자주 들어요. '패배자'보다 지치고 초라한 모습이 떠오르는 말이에요.
explain_en: Originally it means a soldier from a defeated army, but in daily life it is often used figuratively for someone downcast after losing an exam or a game. Compared with '패배자' (loser), it suggests a worn-out, shabby look.

examples.ko: 패전국은 전쟁이 끝난 뒤 큰 빚을 졌어요.
examples.en: The defeated country took on huge debts after the war ended.
We learned about the defeated country in history class.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 두 번의 세계 전쟁에서 패전국이 되었어요.
examples.en: That country ended up on the losing side in both world wars.
It was common to demand reparations from defeated countries.
The positions of the defeated and victorious countries were completely different.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 패전국 사람들의 삶을 그리고 있어요.
examples.en: This novel portrays the lives of people in a defeated nation.

explain: 반대말은 '승전국'이고, '전승국'이라고도 해요. 주로 역사 수업이나 뉴스에서 나오는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 자주 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: The opposite is '승전국' (victorious country), also called '전승국'. It mostly appears in history lessons and the news, not in everyday conversation.

examples.en: In old offices, people sent documents by fax.

examples.ko: 팩시밀리가 고장 나서 서류를 못 받았어요.
examples.en: The fax machine broke, so I couldn't receive the documents.

examples.ko: 요즘은 팩시밀리 대신 이메일을 많이 써요.
examples.en: These days people use email instead of fax a lot.

examples.ko: 이 팩시밀리는 번호를 누르면 바로 전송돼요.
examples.en: This fax machine sends right away once you dial the number.
I went to send a fax to the bank.
The office fax machine has run out of paper.

explain: 보통은 줄여서 '팩스'라고 해요. '팩스를 보내다/받다'처럼 말하고, '팩시밀리'는 글이나 기계 이름을 정확히 말할 때 더 어울려요.
explain_en: People usually shorten it to '팩스'. You say '팩스를 보내다/받다' (send/receive a fax), and '팩시밀리' fits better in writing or when naming the machine formally.

examples.ko: 봄이 되면 화단에 팬지가 가득 피어요.
examples.en: In spring, pansies bloom all over the flower bed.
I bought a pot of purple pansies.

examples.ko: 팬지는 추위에 강해서 이른 봄에도 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Pansies handle the cold well, so you can see them in early spring.
My friend shared some pansy seeds with me.
I watered the pansies I put by the window.

examples.ko: 노란 팬지와 보라색 꽃이 나란히 피었어요.
examples.en: Yellow pansies and purple flowers bloomed side by side.

explain: '삼색제비꽃'이라고도 부르는 꽃이에요. 화분이나 화단에 심는 봄꽃으로 많이 알려져 있어요.
explain_en: It is also called '삼색제비꽃'. It is known as a spring flower planted in pots and flower beds.

examples.en: Tears welled up in my eyes, but I held them back.
The child laughed as he spun the top round and round.
The leaves fell, twirling in the wind.

examples.ko: 피겨 선수가 팽그르르 한 바퀴를 돌았어요.
examples.en: The figure skater spun around once in a quick twirl.
The coin spun around and then stopped.
The chair spun around, and I felt dizzy.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 빠르게 한 바퀴 도는 모양을 나타내요. '빙그르르', '뱅그르르'도 비슷하게 도는 모양인데 느낌이 조금씩 달라요. 눈물이 고일 때도 '눈물이 팽그르르 돌다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It describes something small and light spinning quickly. '빙그르르' and '뱅그르르' also describe spinning, with slightly different feels. It is also used for welling tears: '눈물이 팽그르르 돌다'.

examples.ko: 요즘 불신 풍조의 팽배가 문제라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the spread of distrust these days is a problem.

examples.ko: 경쟁 심리의 팽배는 학생들에게 부담을 줘요.
examples.en: The prevalence of a competitive mindset puts pressure on students.
The news pointed out the spread of selfishness.

examples.ko: 이런 분위기의 팽배는 하루아침에 생기지 않아요.
examples.en: The spread of this kind of atmosphere doesn't happen overnight.
The market froze because of the surge in anxiety.
Let's look for the cause of the growing conflict together.

explain: 보통 '팽배하다' 형태로 더 많이 쓰고, 명사 '팽배'는 '~의 팽배'처럼 글에서 나와요. 불신, 긴장, 이기주의 같은 부정적인 분위기와 자주 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is more often used as the verb '팽배하다'; the noun '팽배' appears in writing in patterns like '~의 팽배'. It often goes with negative moods such as distrust, tension and selfishness.

examples.ko: 요즘 우리 사회에는 불신이 너무 팽배해요.
examples.en: These days distrust is far too widespread in our society.

examples.ko: 회사 안에 긴장감이 팽배해서 말하기가 어려웠어요.
examples.en: Tension filled the company, so it was hard to speak up.
I want to change the atmosphere where selfishness is rampant.
Anxiety ran high ahead of the election.

examples.ko: 그런 생각이 팽배하면 서로 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: If that kind of thinking spreads, it's hard to trust each other.

examples.ko: 학교에 경쟁 의식이 팽배하지 않도록 노력해요.
examples.en: We try to keep a sense of competition from taking over the school.

explain: 어떤 기운이나 분위기가 사회나 집단에 가득 퍼져 있을 때 써요. 주로 뉴스나 글에서 불신, 긴장, 불안 같은 분위기를 말할 때 나오고, '팽배한 분위기'처럼 명사를 꾸미는 형태도 많아요.
explain_en: It is used when a feeling or atmosphere fills a society or group. It mostly appears in news and writing about distrust, tension or anxiety, often in the modifying form like '팽배한 분위기'.

examples.en: The two teams are evenly matched.
Please pull the rope tight and tie it.

examples.ko: 토론에서 두 사람의 의견이 팽팽히 맞섰어요.
examples.en: The two people's opinions clashed evenly in the debate.
The clothesline is pulled taut.
The score stayed neck and neck throughout the match.

examples.ko: 북 가죽을 팽팽히 씌워야 소리가 좋아요.
examples.en: You have to stretch the drum skin tight for a good sound.

explain: 줄이나 천이 늘어지지 않게 당겨진 모습에 쓰고, 힘이 비슷해서 아슬아슬한 대결에도 써요. 반대는 '느슨히/느슨하게'예요.
explain_en: It describes ropes or cloth pulled without slack, and also close, evenly matched contests. The opposite is '느슨히/느슨하게' (loosely).

examples.en: Grandfather is scooping water out of the well.

examples.ko: 배 안에 고인 물을 빨리 퍼내야 해요.
examples.en: We have to bail out the water in the boat quickly.
I shoveled out the snow and made a path.

examples.ko: 엄마가 밥솥에서 밥을 한 그릇 퍼냈어요.
examples.en: Mom scooped a bowl of rice out of the rice cooker.
Please ladle out the soup with the big ladle.

examples.ko: 연못의 흙탕물을 다 퍼내면 물고기가 보여요.
examples.en: If you scoop out all the muddy water from the pond, you can see the fish.

explain: '푸다'에 '내다'가 붙어서 안에 있는 것을 떠서 밖으로 빼내는 느낌이 강해요. '푸다'는 '퍼요'처럼 바뀌지만 '퍼내다'는 '퍼내요'로 규칙적으로 써요. 반대로 떠서 안에 넣을 때는 '퍼 담다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It combines '푸다' (to scoop) with '내다', so it stresses taking something out from inside. '푸다' changes to '퍼요', but '퍼내다' is regular: '퍼내요'. To scoop something into a container, say '퍼 담다'.

examples.en: The bird flapped its wings and flew up.

examples.ko: 갓 잡은 물고기가 그물 속에서 퍼덕여요.
examples.en: The freshly caught fish is thrashing in the net.
I heard the sound of a chicken flapping its wings.
The pigeon flapped its wings and then flew far away.
The child splashed his arms and legs in the water.

examples.ko: 새장 속 새가 계속 퍼덕이고 있어요.
examples.en: The bird in the cage keeps fluttering around.

explain: 새의 날개나 물고기의 몸처럼 힘 있게 치고 흔드는 움직임에 써요. '퍼덕거리다'와 비슷하고, 더 작고 가벼운 움직임은 '파닥이다/파닥거리다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It describes wings or a fish's body beating or thrashing with force. It is similar to '퍼덕거리다', and smaller, lighter movements are expressed with '파닥이다/파닥거리다'.

examples.en: A good idea suddenly came to me while I was showering.

examples.ko: 그 사람 이름이 퍼뜩 떠오르지 않아요.
examples.en: That person's name just won't come to me right away.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 퍼뜩 정신이 들었어요.
examples.en: Hearing that, I suddenly came to my senses.
I dozed off on the subway and suddenly opened my eyes.
The promise from last night suddenly crossed my mind.

examples.ko: 길을 걷다 퍼뜩 우산을 놓고 온 게 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: Walking down the street, it suddenly hit me that I had left my umbrella behind.

explain: 생각이 갑자기 떠오르거나 정신이 갑자기 들 때 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '문득', '번뜩'이 있고, 보통 '퍼뜩 떠오르다/생각나다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is often used when a thought pops up or you suddenly come to your senses. Similar words are '문득' and '번뜩', and it usually pairs with verbs like '퍼뜩 떠오르다/생각나다'.

examples.en: The caught fish is flopping around on the ground.
I was so startled that my heart pounded.
The fish on the cutting board flopped around and then went still.

examples.ko: 갓 잡은 숭어가 통 안에서 펄떡거렸어요.
examples.en: The freshly caught mullet leapt about in the tub.
It was hard to catch the flopping fish by hand.
The fish in the tank flopped around, so water splashed.

explain: 살아 있는 물고기처럼 힘 있게 뛰고 몸을 튕기는 모습에 주로 써요. 더 작고 가벼운 움직임은 '팔딱거리다'를 쓰고, 심장이 뛰는 모습에도 쓰지만 일상에서는 '두근거리다'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: It mostly describes something lively like a live fish jumping and flopping with force. A smaller, lighter movement is '팔딱거리다'. It can describe a heartbeat, but in daily talk '두근거리다' is more usual.

en: keep waving; keep flapping; keep fluttering

examples.en: The flag in front of the school is flapping in the wind.
The laundry is fluttering on the line.
The curtain fluttered by the window.
The wind is strong, so the tent keeps flapping.
The coat tails flapping in the wind look cool.
The big banner flapped for a while and then fell down.

explain: 깃발, 빨래, 커튼처럼 얇고 가벼운 것이 바람에 계속 흔들리는 모습에 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '펄럭이다'를 더 많이 말하고, '펄럭거리다'는 흔들림이 계속되는 느낌이 조금 더 있어요.
explain_en: It describes thin, light things like flags, laundry and curtains waving continuously in the wind. People also say '펄럭이다' for the same idea, while '펄럭거리다' adds a slightly stronger sense of repeated movement.

examples.en: These pants are loose around the waist, so they're comfortable.
I stayed home wearing a baggy T-shirt.

examples.ko: 이 치마 입으면 엉덩이가 펑퍼짐해 보이지 않아요?
examples.en: Doesn't my hip look wide when I wear this skirt?
That dress is too baggy.
As I got older, my figure became broader and rounder.

examples.ko: 옷을 펑퍼짐하게 입으면 더 커 보여요.
examples.en: If you wear baggy clothes, you look bigger.

explain: 옷이 헐렁하고 넉넉할 때, 또 엉덩이나 몸이 옆으로 넓고 둥글게 퍼져 있을 때 써요. 사람의 몸에 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있으니 남에게는 조심해서 말해요.
explain_en: It describes clothes that are loose and roomy, or a body or hips that spread wide and round. Using it about someone's body can be rude, so be careful when talking about other people.

examples.ko: 펜대를 너무 세게 쥐면 손이 아파요.
examples.en: If you grip the pen too hard, your hand hurts.
This pen holder is thick, so it's comfortable to hold.
There is ink on the end of the pen holder.
Grandfather wrote with an old pen holder.

examples.ko: 친구 이름을 새긴 펜대를 선물 포장했어요.
examples.en: I gift-wrapped a pen holder engraved with my friend's name.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 펜대만 굴리다 보니 어깨가 아파요.
examples.en: After pushing a pen all day, my shoulders hurt.

explain: 펜촉을 끼워 쓰는 옛날식 펜에서 손으로 잡는 대를 가리켜요. 요즘은 '펜대를 굴리다'라는 관용 표현으로 더 자주 들어요. 몸으로 하는 일과 달리 책상에서 글을 쓰거나 서류를 다루는 일을 가리킬 때 써요.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 펜대를 굴리는 일이라 어깨가 아파요.
phrases.en: It's a job of pushing a pen all day, so my shoulders hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸을 쓰지 않고 글을 쓰거나 서류를 다루는 사무직 일을 한다는 뜻이에요. 몸 쓰는 일과 비교하며 조금 가볍게 말할 때도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means doing desk work, writing or handling papers instead of physical labor. It is sometimes said a bit lightly in contrast with manual work.

explain_en: It is the holder you grip on an old-style dip pen with a replaceable nib. Today it is more often heard in the idiom '펜대를 굴리다', which refers to desk work with writing or papers, as opposed to physical labor.

examples.ko: 책 뒤쪽에 펴낸이의 이름이 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The publisher's name is written at the back of the book.
The publisher of this book is the head of the publishing house.
I sent a letter directly to the publisher.

examples.ko: 지은이와 펴낸이가 같은 사람일 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes the author and the publisher are the same person.

examples.ko: 판권 면에서 펴낸이와 찍은 날짜를 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked the publisher and the printing date on the copyright page.
I ordered the book through the publisher's contact information.

explain: 책 맨 뒤 판권 면에 '지은이', '펴낸이'가 함께 적혀 있어요. '지은이'는 쓴 사람이고 '펴낸이'는 책을 내는 사람이나 회사 대표라서 둘이 달라요. 한자어로는 '발행인'이라고 해요.
explain_en: On the copyright page at the back of a book, '지은이' and '펴낸이' are listed together. '지은이' is the writer and '펴낸이' is the person or company head who puts the book out, so they differ. The Sino-Korean word is '발행인'.

examples.ko: 목이 너무 아파서 병원에 갔더니 편도선염이래요.
examples.en: My throat hurt so much that I went to the hospital, and they said it's tonsillitis.
I caught tonsillitis and ran a high fever.
Because of tonsillitis, it's hard to swallow food.

examples.ko: 아이가 편도선염으로 며칠 학교에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: My child couldn't go to school for a few days because of tonsillitis.

examples.ko: 편도선염이 자주 생기면 수술을 생각해 볼 수도 있대요.
examples.en: They say if you get tonsillitis often, you may consider surgery.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 편도선염은 푹 쉬어야 낫는다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said tonsillitis gets better only if you rest well.

explain: '편도염'이라고도 말해요. 목이 아프고 열이 날 때 병원에서 자주 듣는 병명이고, 보통 '편도선염에 걸리다'라고 말해요. 발음은 [편도선념]으로 'ㄴ'이 덧나요.
explain_en: It is also called '편도염'. It is a diagnosis you may hear at the clinic with a sore throat and fever, and you say '편도선염에 걸리다' (come down with it). It is pronounced [편도선념], with an added 'ㄴ' sound.

examples.en: Korea is strongly affected by the westerlies.

examples.ko: 편서풍이 불어서 구름이 서쪽에서 동쪽으로 움직여요.
examples.en: The westerlies blow, so clouds move from west to east.

examples.ko: 편서풍 때문에 비행기가 동쪽으로 갈 때 더 빨라요.
examples.en: Because of the westerlies, planes are faster when flying east.
The westerlies are winds that blow in the mid-latitudes.
In geography class we compared the westerlies and the trade winds.
Yellow dust rides the westerlies and reaches Korea.

explain: 중위도 지방에서 주로 서쪽에서 동쪽으로 부는 바람이에요. 한국의 날씨가 서쪽에서 동쪽으로 바뀌는 까닭이나 황사가 오는 까닭을 설명할 때 자주 나와요. 열대 지방에서 동쪽에서 서쪽으로 부는 '무역풍'과 방향이 반대예요.
explain_en: It is a wind that blows mainly from west to east in the mid-latitudes. It often appears when explaining why weather in Korea moves from west to east or why yellow dust arrives. It is opposite in direction to the '무역풍' (trade winds) that blow from east to west in the tropics.

examples.en: Sliced boiled meat was on the New Year's table.
I dipped the sliced boiled meat in salted shrimp and ate it.

examples.ko: 편육은 차게 식혀서 썰어야 잘 썰려요.
examples.en: Boiled pressed meat slices well when you cool it first.
I was given a plate of sliced boiled meat at the party house.
Sliced boiled meat is tasty with kimchi.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 편육도 맛있고 국밥도 맛있어요.
examples.en: This restaurant has tasty boiled meat slices and tasty soup with rice.

explain: 삶은 고기를 눌러서 식힌 뒤 얇게 썬 음식이에요. 명절이나 잔치 음식으로 자주 나오고, 보통 새우젓이나 초간장에 찍어 먹어요. 소고기뿐 아니라 돼지고기로도 만들어요.
explain_en: It is boiled meat that is pressed, cooled and thinly sliced. It often appears at holidays and feasts, usually dipped in salted shrimp or vinegar-soy sauce. It can be made from pork as well as beef.

examples.en: I entered the university this year as a transfer student.

examples.ko: 편입생은 학점 인정 절차를 먼저 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: Transfer students need to check the credit recognition process first.

examples.ko: 우리 반에 편입생이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are two transfer students in our class.
An information session for transfer students is being held.
My transfer student friend says the school still feels unfamiliar.
Some schools give scholarships to transfer students.

explain: 주로 대학에서 다른 학교나 학과에서 옮겨 온 학생을 말해요. 초·중·고등학교에서는 보통 '전학생'이라고 하고, 처음 입학한 학생은 '신입생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It mainly refers to a student who moved into a university from another school or major. In elementary through high school, people usually say '전학생', and a first-time entrant is a '신입생'.
